channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Japanese Yen hangs near four-decade low as bears turn cautious amid intervention risks
item.description: The USD/JPY pair seesaws between tepid gains/minor losses during the Asian session on Monday and currently trades just below mid-162.00s amid relatively thin liquidity on the back of a holiday in Japan.

item.title: US President Donald Trump says US hitting Iran 'very hard’
item.description: US President Donald Trump said that the latest US strikes on Iran were being carried out in honour of US service members killed in recent days, the Guardian reported on Monday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar remains subdued following PBoC policy decision
item.description: NZD/USD remains in negative territory for the third consecutive day, trading around 0.5840 during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: British Pound holds steady near 1.3450 as US-Iran strikes intensify
item.description: The GBP/USD pair trades on a flat note around 1.3450 during the early Asian session on Monday. Traders continue to assess the developments surrounding US-Iran tensions after the US said that a third American troop was killed in the past two days.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7948 vs. 6.7934 previous
item.description: On Monday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7948 compared to Friday's fix of 6.7934 and 6.7577 Reuters estimate.

item.title: PBOC holds Loan Prime Rates steady in July
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC), China's central bank, announced to leave its Loan Prime Rates (LPRs) unchanged on Monday. The one-year and five-year LPRs were at 3.00% and 3.50%, respectively.

item.title: Euro bulls remain on the sidelines as USD gains on US-Iran tensions and inflation fears
item.description: The EUR/USD pair kicks off the new week on a softer note, though it lacks follow-through selling, warranting caution before positioning for an extension of the pullback from a nearly four-week high touched last Wednesday.

item.title: WTI surges above $83.00 amid escalating US-Iran conflict
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price opened at a bullish gap, trading around $83.50 per barrel during the Asian hours on Monday.

item.title: Gold falls toward $4,000 as US-Iran hostilities boosts Fed rate hike bets
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) falls to around $4,000 during the early Asian trading hours on Monday. The precious metal hovers around the psychological level in recent weeks after losing 14% in the second quarter (Q2), its worst showing since 2013.

item.title: Australian Dollar softens below 0.7000 as US–Iran conflicts escalate
item.description: The AUD/USD pair edges lower to around 0.6975 during the early Asian session on Monday. The Australian Dollar (AUD) extends the decline below the 0.7000 psychological level due to escalating tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: US launches airstrikes to ‘swiftly punish’ Iran for deaths of US troops
item.description: The United States (US) has launched the ninth night of Iran strikes. Washington said that airstrikes on Sunday aimed to "punish" Iran over the first US military deaths since renewed hostilities with Tehran, Bloomberg reported.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Consolidation holds upside bias against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) strategists Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/CNH is currently consolidating in a narrow range around 6.77. In their 1–3 week view, they maintain a downside bias toward 6.7600 as long as strong resistance at 6.7820 remains intact.

item.title: South Korea: Faster hiking path – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Ma Tieying analyzes the latest Bank of Korea (BoK) decision, noting a hawkish shift as the base rate is raised to 2.75%. The report now anticipates a faster tightening cycle, with the policy rate reaching 3.25% by year-end 2026.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG hits fresh YTD low, bears eye $54 breakdown
item.description: Silver price recovered some ground on Friday, up 0.84%, but it is poised to finish the week down over 6.50%. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades at $56.00 per troy ounce, after reaching a new year-to-date (YTD) low of $54.77.

item.title: China: Stagnation to persist as growth model shifts – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Henry Hao argues China’s housing market remains in structural stagnation five years after the Evergrande crisis. National prices follow an L-shaped path, with a K-shaped divergence between Tier-1 and lower-tier cities.

item.title: Mexican Peso tumbles as Iran war jitters, denting Peso’s appetite
item.description: The Mexican Peso loses traction against the Greenback, dropping over 0.65% during Friday’s North American session as the American currency benefits due to its safe-haven appeal as the US-Iran conflict is far from ending, despite holding talks to finish the war.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Verbal intervention fails to move JPY against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note USD/JPY is little changed despite strong verbal intervention from Finance Minister Katayama, who warned of decisive action at any time. Markets remain unimpressed, given repeated rhetoric and limited impact from actual Yen buying.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Range trade holds near recent lows against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) strategists Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/SGD has stabilised after an earlier sell-off, with spot around 1.2905 and intraday price action expected to stay confined between nearby support and resistance.

item.title: Forecasting the coming week: ECB decision, UK inflation, and global PMIs to drive markets
item.description: The upcoming week will be dominated by the European Central Bank’s (ECB) interest rate decision, United Kingdom (UK) inflation and labor market figures, and preliminary global Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) data.

item.title: Gold climbs as Iran war premium revives Fed hike risk
item.description: Gold edges higher by some 0.92% on Friday as the US-Iran conflict boosted energy prices, which ultimately drive inflation higher, increasing expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) might need to raise interest rates.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average fades its own good news as the hawks take the last word
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades near 52,250 on Friday, down nearly 300 points late in the month's strangest session.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Bulls pause below 0.8150 as momentum fades
item.description: USD/CHF trades with a downside bias on Friday as the Swiss Franc (CHF) outperforms its major peers, while the US Dollar (USD) is little changed. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 0.8074 after reaching 0.8149 earlier this week, its highest level since August 2025.

item.title: US Dollar Index holds as mixed US data limits upside
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) trades nearly unchanged around 100.70 on Friday after surrendering part of its initial advance.

item.title: Euro steadies as markets weigh ECB and Fed interest rate expectations
item.description: EUR/USD trades flat on Friday as traders reassess the inflationary impact of surging Oil prices amid escalating tensions in the Middle East, which have disrupted energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: British Pound slips for second straight day as Oil spike revives inflation fears
item.description: The Pound Sterling retreats during the North American session, down 0.22% against the Greenback, as geopolitical tensions remained high, triggering a jump in Oil prices and heightening fears of a reacceleration of inflation. The GBP/USD trades at 1.3449 after peaking near 1.3480.

item.title: WTI Oil rallies above $81 as Middle East tensions threaten global Oil supplies
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) trades around $81.10 at the time of writing on Friday, up 2.76% on the day, and is heading for a weekly gain of more than 13% as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East continue to escalate.

item.title: Australian Dollar recovers as mixed US data weakens the US Dollar
item.description: AUD/USD trades higher near 0.6980 on Friday, recovering from an initial decline as the US Dollar (USD) loses ground following a mixed batch of United States (US) economic data.

item.title: British Pound: Burnham policy hopes underpin Sterling against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret notes GBP/USD is lower on the day and well off its one-year high reached on optimism that incoming PM Burnham will pursue market-friendly policies. Despite late-week slippage, that view remains.

item.title: Japanese Yen struggles as higher Oil prices and a wide US-Japan rate gap weigh
item.description: USD/JPY trades flat on Friday, holding near four-decade highs as the Japanese Yen struggles to attract buyers amid persistent headwinds, including higher Oil prices, Japan’s wide interest-rate gap with other major economies and a resilient US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Canada: Inflation divergence shapes BoC outlook – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economists Nathan Janzen and Abbey Xu expect Canada’s June Consumer Price Index to show headline inflation easing to 2.8% year-over-year from 3.2% in May, mainly on lower energy prices.
